274	/** Cached APOD for a date, or null when NASA has not published it yet. */
275	async function fetchApod(log: string[], devFlags: DevFlags, date: string): Promise<Apod | null> {
276	  // Dev fixture short-circuit: only for today's date, bypasses cache entirely
277	  // so fixture runs never pollute real cached data.
278	  if (devFlags.enabled && devFlags.mode && date === todayET()) {
279	    const fixture = devApodFixture(devFlags.mode, date);
280	    if (fixture) {
281	      log.push(`  [fetchApod] ${date} → dev fixture (${devFlags.mode})`);
282	      return fixture;
283	    }
284	  }
285	
286	  const cache = caches.default;
287	  const cacheReq = new Request(apodCacheUrl(date));
288	  const staleReq = new Request(apodCacheUrl(`${date}:stale`));
289	
290	  // nasa-error bypasses the primary cache so every request exercises the
291	  // stale fallback path rather than hitting warm data.
292	  const bypassCache = devFlags.enabled && devFlags.mode === "nasa-error";
293	
294	  if (!bypassCache) {
295	    const cached = await cache.match(cacheReq);
296	    if (cached) {
297	      log.push(`  [fetchApod] ${date} → cache HIT`);
298	      return cached.json() as Promise<Apod>;
299	    }
300	  }
301	
302	  // Deduplicate concurrent requests for the same date
303	  const inflight = inflightApod.get(date);
304	  if (inflight) {
305	    log.push(`  [fetchApod] ${date} → coalesced with in-flight request`);
306	    return inflight;
307	  }
308	
309	  const promise = fetchApodFromUpstream(log, devFlags, date, cacheReq, staleReq);
310	  inflightApod.set(date, promise);
311	  try {
312	    return await promise;
313	  } finally {
314	    inflightApod.delete(date);
315	  }
316	}
317	
318	async function handleUpstreamFailure(
319	  log: string[], cache: Cache, staleReq: Request, date: string, reason: string,
320	): Promise<Apod> {
321	  // Stale cache is the only fallback. The HTML scrape that used to follow it
322	  // was removed in EPIC-0006: NASA's old APOD site redirects every page to
323	  // the science.nasa.gov index now.
324	  const stale = await cache.match(staleReq);
325	  if (stale) {
326	    log.push(`  [fetchApod] ${date} → stale cache fallback (${reason})`);
327	    return stale.json() as Promise<Apod>;
328	  }
329	
330	  throw new Error(`APOD source failed: ${reason}`);
331	}
332	
333	async function fetchApodFromUpstream(
334	  log: string[], devFlags: DevFlags, date: string, cacheReq: Request, staleReq: Request,
335	): Promise<Apod | null> {
336	  const cache = caches.default;
337	
338	  if (devFlags.enabled && devFlags.mode === "nasa-error") {
339	    log.push(`  [fetchApod] ${date} → dev simulated nasa-error (skipping upstream)`);
340	    return handleUpstreamFailure(log, cache, staleReq, date, "simulated by ?dev=nasa-error");
341	  }
342	
343	  // apod-basic keys entries by YYMMDD, like the old apYYMMDD.html pages did.
344	  const yymmdd = date.slice(2).replaceAll("-", "");
345	  const res = await fetch(`${APOD_BASIC_URL}/${yymmdd}?_fields=${APOD_BASIC_FIELDS}`, {
346	    headers: { "User-Agent": USER_AGENT },
347	  });
348	  log.push(`  [fetchApod] ${date} → ${res.status}`);
349	
350	  if (res.status === 404) {
351	    const body = await res.json().catch(() => null) as { code?: string } | null;
352	    if (body?.code === "apod_basic_not_found") {
353	      // Not published yet (NASA posts at 00:05 ET). Not an outage, and
354	      // nothing to cache: the walkback serves the previous day.
355	      log.push(`  [fetchApod] ${date} → not published`);
356	      return null;
357	    }
358	    return handleUpstreamFailure(log, cache, staleReq, date, `404 ${JSON.stringify(body)}`);
359	  }
360	
361	  if (!res.ok) {
362	    const body = (await res.text()).slice(0, 200);
363	    log.push(`  [fetchApod] body=${body}`);
364	    return handleUpstreamFailure(log, cache, staleReq, date, `status ${res.status}`);
365	  }
366	
367	  let apod: Apod;
368	  try {
369	    apod = normalizeApod(await res.json(), date);
370	  } catch (err) {
371	    const msg = err instanceof Error ? err.message : "unknown";
372	    return handleUpstreamFailure(log, cache, staleReq, date, msg);
373	  }
374	
375	  await writeApodCaches(cache, cacheReq, staleReq, apod);
376	  return apod;
377	}
378	
379	async function findLatestResolvable(log: string[], devFlags: DevFlags): Promise<ResolvedApod> {
380	  let unresolvable = 0;
381	  let errors = 0;
382	
383	  for (let i = 0; i <= MAX_LOOKBACK_DAYS; i++) {
384	    const d = new Date();
385	    d.setDate(d.getDate() - i);
386	    const date = d.toLocaleDateString("en-CA", { timeZone: "America/New_York" });
387	
388	    try {
389	      const apod = await fetchApod(log, devFlags, date);
390	      const resolved = apod && resolveApod(apod);
391	      if (resolved) {
392	        if (i > 0 || resolved.source !== "image") {
393	          log.push(`  [findLatest] ${date} → ${resolved.source} (lookback=${i})`);
394	        }
395	        return resolved;
396	      }
397	      unresolvable++;
398	    } catch (err) {
399	      errors++;
400	      const msg = err instanceof Error ? err.message : "unknown";
401	      log.push(`  [findLatest] ${date} → error, skipping (${msg})`);
402	    }
403	  }
404	
405	  throw new Error(
406	    `No image found in last ${MAX_LOOKBACK_DAYS + 1} days (${unresolvable} unresolvable, ${errors} errors)`,
407	  );
408	}

410	// Only APOD photography is ever fetched. Everything the proxy serves comes
411	// through normalizeApod, so this is defense in depth against a bad cache entry.
412	function validateImageUrl(url: string): void {
413	  if (!apodAssetPath(url)) {
414	    throw new Error(`Blocked image fetch: not an APOD asset (${url.slice(0, 80)})`);
415	  }
416	}

418	/**
419	 * Try each image URL in order and return the first that serves. The HD
420	 * original is derived from NASA's hdurl, so hdurl itself is the fallback.
421	 */
422	// ponytail: a 404 on the original is re-paid on every request before the
423	// cached fallback hits. Add a short negative cache if that shows up in logs.
424	async function firstThatServes<T>(
425	  log: string[], urls: string[], attempt: (url: string) => Promise<T>,
426	): Promise<T> {
427	  let lastErr: unknown = new Error("no image candidates");
428	  for (const url of new Set(urls)) {
429	    try {
430	      return await attempt(url);
431	    } catch (err) {
432	      lastErr = err;
433	      log.push(`  [image] ${url.slice(0, 80)}… → ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : "unknown"}`);
434	    }
435	  }
436	  throw lastErr;
437	}

439	async function fetchImageCached(log: string[], url: string): Promise<Response> {
440	  validateImageUrl(url);
441	
442	  const cache = caches.default;
443	  const cacheReq = new Request(`${CACHE_BASE}/image/${encodeURIComponent(url)}`);
444	  const staleReq = new Request(`${CACHE_BASE}/image/${encodeURIComponent(url)}:stale`);
445	
446	  const cached = await cache.match(cacheReq);
447	  if (cached) {
448	    log.push(`  [fetchImage] ${url.slice(0, 80)}… → cache HIT`);
449	    return cached;
450	  }
451	
452	  const res = await fetch(url);
453	
454	  log.push(`  [fetchImage] ${url.slice(0, 80)}… → ${res.status}`);
455	
456	  if (!res.ok) {
457	    // Try stale cache before giving up
458	    const stale = await cache.match(staleReq);
459	    if (stale) {
460	      log.push(`  [fetchImage] ${url.slice(0, 80)}… → stale cache fallback`);
461	      return stale;
462	    }
463	    throw new Error(`Image fetch failed: ${res.status}`);
464	  }
465	
466	  const contentType = res.headers.get("Content-Type") || "image/jpeg";
467	  const contentLength = res.headers.get("Content-Length");
468	  const cacheHeaders: Record<string, string> = {
469	    "Content-Type": contentType,
470	    "Cache-Control": `public, max-age=${CACHE_TTL}`,
471	  };
472	  if (contentLength) cacheHeaders["Content-Length"] = contentLength;
473	
474	  const staleCacheHeaders = { ...cacheHeaders, "Cache-Control": `public, max-age=${STALE_CACHE_TTL}` };
475	
476	  const arrayBuffer = await res.arrayBuffer();
477	  await Promise.all([
478	    cache.put(cacheReq, new Response(arrayBuffer, { headers: cacheHeaders })),
479	    cache.put(staleReq, new Response(arrayBuffer, { headers: staleCacheHeaders })),
480	  ]);
481	  return new Response(arrayBuffer, { headers: cacheHeaders });
482	}

533	      })),

536	  } catch (err) {
537	    log.push(`  [dimensions] ${imageUrl.slice(0, 80)}… → error: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : "unknown"}`);

544	function baseHeaders(origin: string, headers: Record<string, string> = {}): Record<string, string> {
545	  return {
546	    "Access-Control-Allow-Origin": "*",
547	    "Cache-Control": `public, max-age=${CACHE_TTL}`,
548	    "X-Content-Type-Options": "nosniff",
549	    "Link": [
550	      `<${origin}/>; rel="alternate"; type="image/*"; title="HD image"`,
551	      `<${origin}/sd>; rel="alternate"; type="image/*"; title="SD image"`,
552	      `<${origin}/optimized>; rel="alternate"; type="image/*"; title="Optimized image"`,
553	      `<${origin}/thumb>; rel="alternate"; type="image/webp"; title="Thumbnail"`,
554	      `<${origin}/info>; rel="describedby"`,
555	      `<${origin}/about>; rel="about"`,
556	    ].join(", "),
557	    ...headers,
558	  };
559	}

11	 *   GET /optimized → optimized image (≤1200px, auto WebP/AVIF)
12	 *   GET /thumb     → tiny thumbnail (32px, blurred WebP)
13	 *   GET /info      → JSON metadata (includes image dimensions)
14	 *   GET /about     → plain-text description and attribution
15	 */
16	
17	import { z } from "zod";
18	
19	export interface Env {
20	  ENVIRONMENT?: string;
21	}
22	
23	// NASA's APOD feed. A WordPress REST endpoint on science.nasa.gov, keyed by
24	// YYMMDD, no API key. See EPIC-0006 for the verified field behavior.
25	const APOD_BASIC_URL = "https://science.nasa.gov/wp-json/wp/v2/apod-basic";
26	const APOD_BASIC_FIELDS = "date,title,media_type,explanation,copyright,hdurl,permalink,basic_html";
27	const APOD_ASSET_HOST = "https://assets.science.nasa.gov";
28	const USER_AGENT = "nasa-picture-proxy/1.0 (+https://nasapicture.com)";
29	const MAX_LOOKBACK_DAYS = 7;
30	const CACHE_TTL = 21600;      // 6 hours — APOD changes once/day
31	const STALE_CACHE_TTL = 86400; // 24 hours — fallback when the APOD source is down
32	
33	// Prefix for every cache key. Bump the version whenever the cached shape or
34	// the upstream source changes; old keys are never read again and expire on
35	// their own. The host must be in our zone or caches.default drops the write.
36	const CACHE_BASE = "https://api.nasapicture.com/_cache/v2";
37	
38	// Upstream record, trimmed by `_fields`. Only what the proxy cannot work
39	// without is required; everything else degrades to empty.
40	const ApodBasic = z.object({
41	  date: z.string(),
42	  title: z.string().trim().min(1),
43	  media_type: z.enum(["image", "video"]),
44	  explanation: z.string().nullish(),
45	  copyright: z.string().nullish(),
46	  hdurl: z.string().nullish(),
47	  permalink: z.string().nullish(),
48	  basic_html: z.string().nullish(),
49	});
50	
51	export interface ApodImage {
52	  sd: string;         // 1280px rendition (dynamicimage path, no params)
53	  hd: string;         // original bytes (content/dam path)
54	  hdFallback: string; // hdurl as NASA sent it, in case the original is missing
55	}
56	
57	// Normalized, plain-text model. This is what gets cached.
58	export interface Apod {
59	  date: string;
60	  title: string;
61	  explanation: string;
62	  copyright: string | null;
63	  media_type: "image" | "video";
64	  permalink: string;
65	  image: ApodImage | null; // null only on video days without a usable poster
66	  video_url: string | null;
67	}
68	
69	export type ImageSource = "image" | "video_thumbnail";
70	
71	export interface ResolvedApod {
72	  apod: Apod;
73	  image: ApodImage;
74	  source: ImageSource;
75	}
76	
77	export interface DevFlags {
78	  enabled: boolean;
79	  mode: string | null;
80	  tools: Set<string>;
81	}
82	
83	const inflightApod = new Map<string, Promise<Apod | null>>();
84	
85	/** Test-only: clear the in-flight promise map between test cases. */
86	export function __resetInflightApod(): void {
87	  inflightApod.clear();
88	}

90	// ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
91	// Dev flag fixtures — only reachable when env.ENVIRONMENT === "development".
92	// Registered in REFE-0001. When a new mode is added here, update that table.
93	// ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
94	const DEV_POSTER_PATH = "science/cds/apod/apod/2026/october/SonifiedEagleNebulaPillars.jpg";
95	
96	const VIDEO_FIXTURE: Apod = {
97	  date: "2026-10-18",
98	  title: "Fixture: Video APOD (dev=video)",
99	  explanation:
100	    "Dev fixture used to exercise the video-poster branch locally. " +
101	    "Shape mirrors a normalized apod-basic video entry. " +
102	    "See TASK-0019, TASK-0042 and REFE-0001 for context.",
103	  copyright: null,
104	  media_type: "video",
105	  permalink: "https://science.nasa.gov/image-article/apod-2026-october-18-sonified-eagle-nebula-pillars/",
106	  image: {
107	    sd: `${APOD_ASSET_HOST}/dynamicimage/assets/${DEV_POSTER_PATH}`,
108	    hd: `${APOD_ASSET_HOST}/content/dam/${DEV_POSTER_PATH}`,
109	    hdFallback: `${APOD_ASSET_HOST}/dynamicimage/assets/${DEV_POSTER_PATH}?w=3048&h=1708`,
110	  },
111	  video_url: "https://www.youtube.com/embed/DzrCEm1ZBRY",
112	};
113	
114	const VIDEO_FIXTURE_NO_POSTER: Apod = {
115	  ...VIDEO_FIXTURE,
116	  title: "Fixture: Video APOD no poster (dev=video-no-thumb)",
117	  image: null,
118	  video_url: `${APOD_ASSET_HOST}/content/dam/science/cds/apod/apod/2026/october/CRS35-Holland30s1080p.mp4`,
119	};
120	
121	export function devApodFixture(mode: string, date: string): Apod | null {
122	  if (mode === "video") return { ...VIDEO_FIXTURE, date };
123	  if (mode === "video-no-thumb") return { ...VIDEO_FIXTURE_NO_POSTER, date };
124	  return null;
125	}
126	
127	export function parseDevFlags(url: URL, env: Env): DevFlags {
128	  const enabled = env.ENVIRONMENT === "development";
129	  if (!enabled) {
130	    return { enabled: false, mode: null, tools: new Set() };
131	  }
132	  const rawMode = url.searchParams.get("dev");
133	  const mode = rawMode && rawMode !== "off" && rawMode !== "" ? rawMode : null;
134	  const toolsCsv = url.searchParams.get("tools");
135	  const tools = new Set(
136	    toolsCsv
137	      ? toolsCsv.split(",").map((s) => s.trim()).filter(Boolean)
138	      : [],
139	  );
140	  return { enabled, mode, tools };
141	}
142	
143	// ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
144	// Upstream normalization
145	// ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
146	
147	// APOD photography lives under one asset tree. Anything else on the host
148	// (site chrome, the generic news thumbnail, videos) is not an APOD image.
149	const APOD_ASSET_PATH =
150	  /^\/(?:dynamicimage\/assets|content\/dam)\/(science\/cds\/apod\/.+\.(?:jpe?g|png|gif|webp))$/i;
151	
152	/** Asset path under assets.science.nasa.gov, or null when the URL points anywhere else. */
153	export function apodAssetPath(url: string): string | null {
154	  let parsed: URL;
155	  try {
156	    parsed = new URL(url);
157	  } catch {
158	    return null;
159	  }
160	  if (parsed.protocol !== "https:" || parsed.hostname !== "assets.science.nasa.gov") return null;
161	  return parsed.pathname.match(APOD_ASSET_PATH)?.[1] ?? null;
162	}
163	
164	function apodImage(url: string): ApodImage | null {
165	  const path = apodAssetPath(url);
166	  if (!path) return null;
167	  return {
168	    sd: `${APOD_ASSET_HOST}/dynamicimage/assets/${path}`,
169	    hd: `${APOD_ASSET_HOST}/content/dam/${path}`,
170	    hdFallback: url,
171	  };
172	}
173	
174	// basic_html is the legacy APOD page layout. It is the only place the video
175	// embed lives, and the only place the real image lives when hdurl is the
176	// generic placeholder thumbnail (some older entries).
177	function imageFromHtml(html: string): ApodImage | null {
178	  for (const m of html.matchAll(/(?:href|src|poster)="([^"]+)"/gi)) {
179	    const image = apodImage(m[1].replace(/&amp;/gi, "&"));
180	    if (image) return image;
181	  }
182	  return null;
183	}
184	
185	function videoUrlFromHtml(html: string): string | null {
186	  const m = html.match(/<iframe[^>]+src="([^"]+)"/i) ?? html.match(/<source[^>]+src="([^"]+)"/i);
187	  if (!m) return null;
188	  const src = m[1].replace(/&amp;/gi, "&");
189	  return src.startsWith("//") ? `https:${src}` : src;
190	}
191	
192	function stripHtml(s: string): string {
193	  return s
194	    .replace(/<br\s*\/?>|<\/p>/gi, " ")
195	    .replace(/<[^>]+>/g, "")
196	    .replace(/&nbsp;/gi, " ")
197	    .replace(/&amp;/gi, "&")
198	    .replace(/&quot;/gi, '"')
199	    .replace(/&#39;/gi, "'")
200	    .replace(/&lt;/gi, "<")
201	    .replace(/&gt;/gi, ">")
202	    .replace(/\s+/g, " ")
203	    .trim();
204	}
205	
206	/**
207	 * Validate an apod-basic record and map it to the internal model. Throws on
208	 * anything that must never be cached or served: schema failures, a record
209	 * for a different date, or an image day with no APOD image (the 2026-10-20
210	 * logo outage looked exactly like that).
211	 */
212	export function normalizeApod(raw: unknown, date: string): Apod {
213	  const parsed = ApodBasic.safeParse(raw);
214	  if (!parsed.success) {
215	    throw new Error(`invalid record: ${z.prettifyError(parsed.error)}`);
216	  }
217	  const rec = parsed.data;
218	  if (rec.date !== date) {
219	    throw new Error(`date mismatch: asked ${date}, got ${rec.date}`);
220	  }
221	
222	  const html = rec.basic_html ?? "";
223	  const image = apodImage(rec.hdurl ?? "") ?? imageFromHtml(html);
224	  if (rec.media_type === "image" && !image) {
225	    throw new Error(`no APOD image in hdurl (${rec.hdurl}) or basic_html`);
226	  }
227	
228	  const copyright = stripHtml(rec.copyright ?? "");
229	  return {
230	    date: rec.date,
231	    title: stripHtml(rec.title),
232	    explanation: stripHtml(rec.explanation ?? "").replace(/^Explanation:\s*/, ""),
233	    copyright: copyright || null,
234	    media_type: rec.media_type,
235	    permalink: rec.permalink ?? "",
236	    image,
237	    video_url: rec.media_type === "video" ? videoUrlFromHtml(html) : null,
238	  };
239	}
240	
241	export function resolveApod(apod: Apod): ResolvedApod | null {
242	  if (!apod.image) return null;
243	  return {
244	    apod,
245	    image: apod.image,
246	    source: apod.media_type === "video" ? "video_thumbnail" : "image",
247	  };
248	}
249	
250	// ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
251	// Fetch and cache
252	// ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
253	
254	export function apodCacheUrl(key: string): string {
255	  return `${CACHE_BASE}/apod/${key}`;
256	}
257	
258	function todayET(): string {
259	  return new Date().toLocaleDateString("en-CA", { timeZone: "America/New_York" });
260	}
261	
262	async function writeApodCaches(
263	  cache: Cache, cacheReq: Request, staleReq: Request, apod: Apod,
264	): Promise<void> {
265	  const body = JSON.stringify(apod);
266	  const cacheHeaders = { "Content-Type": "application/json", "Cache-Control": `public, max-age=${CACHE_TTL}` };
267	  const staleHeaders = { "Content-Type": "application/json", "Cache-Control": `public, max-age=${STALE_CACHE_TTL}` };
268	  await Promise.all([
269	    cache.put(cacheReq, new Response(body, { headers: cacheHeaders })),
270	    cache.put(staleReq, new Response(body, { headers: staleHeaders })),
271	  ]);
272	}
273	
274	/** Cached APOD for a date, or null when NASA has not published it yet. */
275	async function fetchApod(log: string[], devFlags: DevFlags, date: string): Promise<Apod | null> {
276	  // Dev fixture short-circuit: only for today's date, bypasses cache entirely
277	  // so fixture runs never pollute real cached data.
278	  if (devFlags.enabled && devFlags.mode && date === todayET()) {
279	    const fixture = devApodFixture(devFlags.mode, date);
280	    if (fixture) {
281	      log.push(`  [fetchApod] ${date} → dev fixture (${devFlags.mode})`);
282	      return fixture;
283	    }
284	  }
285	
286	  const cache = caches.default;
287	  const cacheReq = new Request(apodCacheUrl(date));
288	  const staleReq = new Request(apodCacheUrl(`${date}:stale`));
289	
290	  // nasa-error bypasses the primary cache so every request exercises the
291	  // stale fallback path rather than hitting warm data.
292	  const bypassCache = devFlags.enabled && devFlags.mode === "nasa-error";
293	
294	  if (!bypassCache) {
295	    const cached = await cache.match(cacheReq);
296	    if (cached) {
297	      log.push(`  [fetchApod] ${date} → cache HIT`);
298	      return cached.json() as Promise<Apod>;
299	    }
300	  }
301	
302	  // Deduplicate concurrent requests for the same date
303	  const inflight = inflightApod.get(date);
304	  if (inflight) {
305	    log.push(`  [fetchApod] ${date} → coalesced with in-flight request`);
306	    return inflight;
307	  }
308	
309	  const promise = fetchApodFromUpstream(log, devFlags, date, cacheReq, staleReq);
310	  inflightApod.set(date, promise);
311	  try {
312	    return await promise;
313	  } finally {
314	    inflightApod.delete(date);
315	  }
316	}
317	
318	async function handleUpstreamFailure(
319	  log: string[], cache: Cache, staleReq: Request, date: string, reason: string,
320	): Promise<Apod> {
321	  // Stale cache is the only fallback. The HTML scrape that used to follow it
322	  // was removed in EPIC-0006: NASA's old APOD site redirects every page to
323	  // the science.nasa.gov index now.
324	  const stale = await cache.match(staleReq);
325	  if (stale) {
326	    log.push(`  [fetchApod] ${date} → stale cache fallback (${reason})`);
327	    return stale.json() as Promise<Apod>;
328	  }
329	
330	  throw new Error(`APOD source failed: ${reason}`);
331	}
332	
333	async function fetchApodFromUpstream(
334	  log: string[], devFlags: DevFlags, date: string, cacheReq: Request, staleReq: Request,
335	): Promise<Apod | null> {
336	  const cache = caches.default;
337	
338	  if (devFlags.enabled && devFlags.mode === "nasa-error") {
339	    log.push(`  [fetchApod] ${date} → dev simulated nasa-error (skipping upstream)`);
340	    return handleUpstreamFailure(log, cache, staleReq, date, "simulated by ?dev=nasa-error");
341	  }
342	
343	  // apod-basic keys entries by YYMMDD, like the old apYYMMDD.html pages did.
344	  const yymmdd = date.slice(2).replaceAll("-", "");
345	  const res = await fetch(`${APOD_BASIC_URL}/${yymmdd}?_fields=${APOD_BASIC_FIELDS}`, {
346	    headers: { "User-Agent": USER_AGENT },
347	  });
348	  log.push(`  [fetchApod] ${date} → ${res.status}`);
349	
350	  if (res.status === 404) {
351	    const body = await res.json().catch(() => null) as { code?: string } | null;
352	    if (body?.code === "apod_basic_not_found") {
353	      // Not published yet (NASA posts at 00:05 ET). Not an outage, and
354	      // nothing to cache: the walkback serves the previous day.
355	      log.push(`  [fetchApod] ${date} → not published`);
356	      return null;
357	    }
358	    return handleUpstreamFailure(log, cache, staleReq, date, `404 ${JSON.stringify(body)}`);
359	  }
360	
361	  if (!res.ok) {
362	    const body = (await res.text()).slice(0, 200);
363	    log.push(`  [fetchApod] body=${body}`);
364	    return handleUpstreamFailure(log, cache, staleReq, date, `status ${res.status}`);
365	  }
366	
367	  let apod: Apod;
368	  try {
369	    apod = normalizeApod(await res.json(), date);
370	  } catch (err) {
371	    const msg = err instanceof Error ? err.message : "unknown";
372	    return handleUpstreamFailure(log, cache, staleReq, date, msg);
373	  }
374	
375	  await writeApodCaches(cache, cacheReq, staleReq, apod);
376	  return apod;
377	}
378	
379	async function findLatestResolvable(log: string[], devFlags: DevFlags): Promise<ResolvedApod> {
380	  let unresolvable = 0;
381	  let errors = 0;
382	
383	  for (let i = 0; i <= MAX_LOOKBACK_DAYS; i++) {
384	    const d = new Date();
385	    d.setDate(d.getDate() - i);
386	    const date = d.toLocaleDateString("en-CA", { timeZone: "America/New_York" });
387	
388	    try {
389	      const apod = await fetchApod(log, devFlags, date);
390	      const resolved = apod && resolveApod(apod);
391	      if (resolved) {
392	        if (i > 0 || resolved.source !== "image") {
393	          log.push(`  [findLatest] ${date} → ${resolved.source} (lookback=${i})`);
394	        }
395	        return resolved;
396	      }
397	      unresolvable++;
398	    } catch (err) {
399	      errors++;
400	      const msg = err instanceof Error ? err.message : "unknown";
401	      log.push(`  [findLatest] ${date} → error, skipping (${msg})`);
402	    }
403	  }
404	
405	  throw new Error(
406	    `No image found in last ${MAX_LOOKBACK_DAYS + 1} days (${unresolvable} unresolvable, ${errors} errors)`,
407	  );
408	}
409	
410	// Only APOD photography is ever fetched. Everything the proxy serves comes
411	// through normalizeApod, so this is defense in depth against a bad cache entry.
412	function validateImageUrl(url: string): void {
413	  if (!apodAssetPath(url)) {
414	    throw new Error(`Blocked image fetch: not an APOD asset (${url.slice(0, 80)})`);
415	  }
416	}
417	
418	/**
419	 * Try each image URL in order and return the first that serves. The HD
420	 * original is derived from NASA's hdurl, so hdurl itself is the fallback.
421	 */
422	// ponytail: a 404 on the original is re-paid on every request before the
423	// cached fallback hits. Add a short negative cache if that shows up in logs.
424	async function firstThatServes<T>(
425	  log: string[], urls: string[], attempt: (url: string) => Promise<T>,
426	): Promise<T> {
427	  let lastErr: unknown = new Error("no image candidates");
428	  for (const url of new Set(urls)) {
429	    try {
430	      return await attempt(url);
431	    } catch (err) {
432	      lastErr = err;
433	      log.push(`  [image] ${url.slice(0, 80)}… → ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : "unknown"}`);
434	    }
435	  }
436	  throw lastErr;
437	}
438	
439	async function fetchImageCached(log: string[], url: string): Promise<Response> {
440	  validateImageUrl(url);
441	
442	  const cache = caches.default;
443	  const cacheReq = new Request(`${CACHE_BASE}/image/${encodeURIComponent(url)}`);
444	  const staleReq = new Request(`${CACHE_BASE}/image/${encodeURIComponent(url)}:stale`);
445	
446	  const cached = await cache.match(cacheReq);
447	  if (cached) {
448	    log.push(`  [fetchImage] ${url.slice(0, 80)}… → cache HIT`);
449	    return cached;
450	  }
451	
452	  const res = await fetch(url);
453	
454	  log.push(`  [fetchImage] ${url.slice(0, 80)}… → ${res.status}`);
455	
456	  if (!res.ok) {
457	    // Try stale cache before giving up
458	    const stale = await cache.match(staleReq);
459	    if (stale) {
460	      log.push(`  [fetchImage] ${url.slice(0, 80)}… → stale cache fallback`);
461	      return stale;
462	    }
463	    throw new Error(`Image fetch failed: ${res.status}`);
464	  }
465	
466	  const contentType = res.headers.get("Content-Type") || "image/jpeg";
467	  const contentLength = res.headers.get("Content-Length");
468	  const cacheHeaders: Record<string, string> = {
469	    "Content-Type": contentType,
470	    "Cache-Control": `public, max-age=${CACHE_TTL}`,
471	  };
472	  if (contentLength) cacheHeaders["Content-Length"] = contentLength;
473	
474	  const staleCacheHeaders = { ...cacheHeaders, "Cache-Control": `public, max-age=${STALE_CACHE_TTL}` };
475	
476	  const arrayBuffer = await res.arrayBuffer();
477	  await Promise.all([
478	    cache.put(cacheReq, new Response(arrayBuffer, { headers: cacheHeaders })),
479	    cache.put(staleReq, new Response(arrayBuffer, { headers: staleCacheHeaders })),
480	  ]);
481	  return new Response(arrayBuffer, { headers: cacheHeaders });
482	}
483	
484	interface ImageDimensions {
485	  width: number;
486	  height: number;
487	}
488	
489	async function fetchImageDimensions(log: string[], imageUrl: string): Promise<ImageDimensions | null> {
490	  validateImageUrl(imageUrl);
491	
492	  const cache = caches.default;
493	  const cacheKey = `${CACHE_BASE}/dimensions/${encodeURIComponent(imageUrl)}`;
494	  const cacheReq = new Request(cacheKey);
495	  const staleReq = new Request(`${cacheKey}:stale`);
496	
497	  const cached = await cache.match(cacheReq);
498	  if (cached) {
499	    log.push(`  [dimensions] ${imageUrl.slice(0, 80)}… → cache HIT`);
500	    return cached.json() as Promise<ImageDimensions>;
501	  }
502	
503	  try {
504	    const res = await fetch(imageUrl, {
505	      cf: { image: { format: "json" } },
506	    });
507	
508	    if (!res.ok) {
509	      const stale = await cache.match(staleReq);
510	      if (stale) {
511	        log.push(`  [dimensions] ${imageUrl.slice(0, 80)}… → stale cache fallback`);
512	        return stale.json() as Promise<ImageDimensions>;
513	      }
514	      log.push(`  [dimensions] ${imageUrl.slice(0, 80)}… → ${res.status} (failed)`);
515	      return null;
516	    }
517	
518	    const info = await res.json() as { original: { width: number; height: number } };
519	    const dimensions: ImageDimensions = {
520	      width: info.original.width,
521	      height: info.original.height,
522	    };
523	
524	    log.push(`  [dimensions] ${imageUrl.slice(0, 80)}… → ${dimensions.width}×${dimensions.height}`);
525	
526	    const body = JSON.stringify(dimensions);
527	    await Promise.all([
528	      cache.put(cacheReq, new Response(body, {
529	        headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json", "Cache-Control": `public, max-age=${CACHE_TTL}` },
530	      })),
531	      cache.put(staleReq, new Response(body, {
532	        headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json", "Cache-Control": `public, max-age=${STALE_CACHE_TTL}` },
533	      })),
534	    ]);
535	    return dimensions;
536	  } catch (err) {
537	    log.push(`  [dimensions] ${imageUrl.slice(0, 80)}… → error: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : "unknown"}`);
538	    const stale = await cache.match(staleReq);
539	    if (stale) return stale.json() as Promise<ImageDimensions>;
540	    return null;
541	  }
542	}
543	
544	function baseHeaders(origin: string, headers: Record<string, string> = {}): Record<string, string> {
545	  return {
546	    "Access-Control-Allow-Origin": "*",
547	    "Cache-Control": `public, max-age=${CACHE_TTL}`,
548	    "X-Content-Type-Options": "nosniff",
549	    "Link": [
550	      `<${origin}/>; rel="alternate"; type="image/*"; title="HD image"`,
551	      `<${origin}/sd>; rel="alternate"; type="image/*"; title="SD image"`,
552	      `<${origin}/optimized>; rel="alternate"; type="image/*"; title="Optimized image"`,
553	      `<${origin}/thumb>; rel="alternate"; type="image/webp"; title="Thumbnail"`,
554	      `<${origin}/info>; rel="describedby"`,
555	      `<${origin}/about>; rel="about"`,
556	    ].join(", "),
557	    ...headers,
558	  };
559	}
560	
561	export default {

# Fetch APOD metadata from the science.nasa.gov apod-basic API

Replace the broken api.nasa.gov source with NASA's new official endpoint, and validate what comes back so a bad upstream response is never cached or served. See EPIC-0006 for the source facts.

## Context

- `fetchApodFromNasa` (`src/index.ts:247-273`) calls `NASA_APOD_URL` (`https://api.nasa.gov/planetary/apod`, line 22) with `api_key` and `date`.
- It casts `res.json() as ApodResponse` (line 270) with no checks, then writes both cache tiers.
- `handleUpstreamFailure` (211-245) only runs on `!res.ok`. A 200 carrying the NASA logo goes straight into the cache.

## Implementation

1. **Fetch.** Replace `NASA_APOD_URL` with `https://science.nasa.gov/wp-json/wp/v2/apod-basic`.
   - Fetch `/${YYMMDD}` with `_fields=date,title,media_type,explanation,copyright,hdurl,permalink,basic_html`.
   - `basic_html` (about 11 KB, cached) is needed by TASK-0043 for video URLs and placeholder entries.
2. **Validate at the boundary** with a Zod 4 schema (add the `zod` dependency, and derive the upstream type with `z.infer`). Reject:
   - a missing or empty `title`
   - a `date` that doesn't match the requested date
   - a `media_type` outside `image` / `video`
3. **Normalize** in one function that maps the upstream record to the internal model.
   - Strip HTML from `explanation` and drop its leading `Explanation:` label.
   - Strip HTML from `copyright`. `stripHtml` (293-304) is reusable.
   - Keep the public `/info` field names (`title`, `date`, `explanation`, `url`, `hdurl`, `media_type`, `copyright`, `image_source`) stable for clients, and add `permalink`.
4. **Status handling:**
   - 404 `apod_basic_not_found` means "not published yet". Treat it as unresolvable so the walkback moves to the previous day. It is not an upstream failure, and nothing is cached for it. This covers the 00:00 to 00:05 ET window before NASA publishes.
   - Any other non-2xx status, or a validation failure, is an upstream failure and goes through `handleUpstreamFailure`.
   - Invalid data is never written to either cache tier.
5. **Remove the API key.** Delete `NASA_API_KEY` (`Env`, line 18), the `DEMO_KEY` fallback (line 598), and the `apiKey` parameter threaded through every fetch function.
   - Make the `NasaApiError` naming and the "NASA API rate limit exceeded…" / "NASA API returned…" messages (242-243) source-neutral.
   - Keep the 429 passthrough only if the new upstream can return 429. None was observed.
6. **User-Agent.** Send a descriptive one; reuse the scrape's `+https://nasapicture.com` UA.
7. **Tests** (`test/handler.test.ts`):
   - Replace `nasaImage()` / `nasaVideoNoThumb()` (161-180) and the `api.nasa.gov/planetary/apod` assertions (263, 331, 450, 494, 497) with apod-basic shapes.
   - Record real responses as fixtures: `261020` (image), `261018` (YouTube video), `261016` (MP4 video), a 404 unpublished date, and a logo-shaped response that must be rejected.

## Acceptance

- No request goes to api.nasa.gov. `NASA_API_KEY` and `DEMO_KEY` are gone from `src/`.
- `/info` for 2026-10-20 returns the title "An Anticrepuscular Rainbow Fan", a plain-text explanation and credit, and `date: 2026-10-20`.
- An unpublished date (404) triggers the walkback, not a 502.
- A response that fails validation is never written to the primary or stale cache, and a test proves it.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm test` pass.

# Resolve APOD image and video URLs from apod-basic data

Map apod-basic's image fields to the bytes each route serves, restore original-resolution HD images, keep video days working, and lock the image allowlist to APOD assets.

## Context

`resolveApod` (`src/index.ts:123-141`) picks `hdurl`/`url` for images and `thumbnail_url` for videos. apod-basic changes all three:

- `url` is now the article permalink, not an image.
- `hdurl` is a re-encoded `dynamicimage` copy. On older or odd entries it is a placeholder PNG, or empty.
- There is no `thumbnail_url`.

`ALLOWED_IMAGE_HOSTS` (28-35) allows any `.nasa.gov` suffix, which is why the logo URL passed.

## Implementation

1. **HD** (`/`, `/image.jpg`): serve the original from `content/dam`.
   - Derive it from `hdurl` by swapping `/dynamicimage/assets/science/` for `/content/dam/science/` and dropping the query. If `hdurl` is already a `content/dam` URL (older eras), just drop the query.
   - If the derived original returns 404, use `hdurl` as given.
2. **SD** (`/sd`, `/image-sd.jpg`): serve the `dynamicimage` path with no params (1280px default).
3. **`/optimized` and `/thumb`:** keep the current `cf.image` options and source selection. Confirm Cloudflare Image Transformations can fetch from `assets.science.nasa.gov`. The 502s seen on 2026-10-20 came from the logo source.
4. **Video:**
   - YouTube day with a poster `hdurl` on assets.science.nasa.gov: serve the poster (`image_source: video_thumbnail`).
   - MP4 day (`hdurl: ""`) or no poster: treat as unresolvable and walk back, which is the existing behavior.
   - Extract the video URL from `basic_html` (`<iframe src="//www.youtube.com/embed/ID">`, normalized to `https:`, or `<video><source src>`) and expose it as `/info` `url` on video days, matching the old API contract.
5. **Placeholders:** if `hdurl` points to `/cosmic-origins/images/misc/news-thumbnail.png`, or any path outside the APOD asset tree, take the real image from `basic_html` (`<a href>` / `<IMG SRC>`). If there is none, the entry is unresolvable.
6. **Tighten `ALLOWED_IMAGE_HOSTS`:** replace the `.nasa.gov` suffix with the exact host `assets.science.nasa.gov`, and require the APOD asset path (`/cds/apod/`), so site chrome like the logo can never pass. Drop `.ytimg.com` / `.youtube.com` / `.vimeocdn.com` if nothing still serves images from them.
7. **Fixtures and tests:** update the dev fixtures `VIDEO_FIXTURE_*` and `devApodFixture` (80-105), the `resolveApod` cases in `test/pure.test.ts` (73-121), and the `?dev=video` / `?dev=video-no-thumb` handler tests to the new shapes.

## Acceptance

- `/` for 2026-10-20 serves the 5120x3840 original (`image/jpeg`, 1,100,460 B).
- `/sd` serves the 1280px rendition.
- 2026-10-18 (YouTube) serves the NASA poster. 2026-10-16 (MP4, no poster) walks back to the previous day.
- The NASA logo URL and the placeholder PNG are rejected, with tests.
- `/info` `width` and `height` are populated for images on the new host.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm test` pass.

# Version cache keys so pre-migration entries are never read

Make the cache key scheme change whenever the cached shape or upstream source changes, so the migration never serves data cached from the old source.

## Context

- **Metadata keys are date-only.** `apodCacheUrl` (`src/index.ts:143-145`) builds `https://api.nasapicture.com/_cache/apod/${date}`, plus a `:stale` variant (180-181).
- **The bad entries outlive a deploy.** The NASA-logo `ApodResponse` cached on 2026-10-20 stays readable for up to 6h in the primary tier and up to 24h in the stale tier.
- **Cache is read before any new code runs.** `fetchApod` (163-209) checks the cache first, so a code fix alone would still serve the logo.
- **Image and dimension caches mostly fix themselves.** They are keyed by upstream URL (`/_cache/image/…` at 452-453, `/_cache/dimensions/…` at 502-504), so they recover once metadata yields new URLs. The logo bytes sit under one shared key, which never needs to be read again.

## Implementation

1. Add a version segment to every `_cache` key (`/_cache/v2/apod/…`, `/_cache/v2/image/…`, `/_cache/v2/dimensions/…`), defined once as a constant. Add a comment at the constant saying to bump it whenever the cached shape or upstream source changes.
2. Don't purge and don't wait for TTLs. Old keys are never read again and expire on their own.
3. Known limit: responses already sent carry `Cache-Control: public, max-age=21600` (`baseHeaders`, 553-568). Browsers and downstream proxies that fetched the logo may keep showing it for up to 6h after deploy. The Worker can't recall those.

## Acceptance

- A test seeds an entry under the old unversioned key and proves it is ignored.
- The key version lives in a single constant used by every cache key.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm test` pass.

4	// ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
5	// In-memory stand-ins for globals the Worker reaches for. Node gives us
6	// Request/Response/fetch/URL natively; we only need to fake `caches.default`
7	// and route outbound `fetch` calls. The tests call the default export's
8	// fetch handler directly — no wrangler, no miniflare, no real network.

11	interface CacheEntry {
12	  body: ArrayBuffer;
13	  headers: [string, string][];
14	}
15	
16	function createCache() {
17	  const store = new Map<string, CacheEntry>();
18	  const cache = {
19	    async match(req: Request | string): Promise<Response | undefined> {
20	      const url = typeof req === "string" ? req : req.url;
21	      const entry = store.get(url);
22	      if (!entry) return undefined;
23	      return new Response(entry.body.slice(0), { headers: entry.headers });
24	    },
25	    async put(req: Request | string, res: Response): Promise<void> {
26	      const url = typeof req === "string" ? req : req.url;
27	      const body = await res.arrayBuffer();
28	      const headers: [string, string][] = [];
29	      res.headers.forEach((value, key) => headers.push([key, value]));
30	      store.set(url, { body, headers });
31	    },
32	    async delete(req: Request | string): Promise<boolean> {
33	      const url = typeof req === "string" ? req : req.url;
34	      return store.delete(url);
35	    },
36	    // helpers for assertions
37	    _keys: () => Array.from(store.keys()),
38	    _size: () => store.size,
39	  };
40	  return cache;
41	}

45	interface FetchCall {

51	type RouteHandler = (req: Request) => Response | Promise<Response>;
52	
53	function createFetchMock() {
54	  const routes: Array<{ match: (url: string) => boolean; handler: RouteHandler }> = [];
55	  const calls: FetchCall[] = [];
56	
57	  const fn: typeof fetch = async (input, init) => {
58	    const req =
59	      input instanceof Request
60	        ? new Request(input, init)
61	        : new Request(typeof input === "string" ? input : String(input), init);
62	    calls.push({ url: req.url, method: req.method, userAgent: req.headers.get("User-Agent") });
63	    for (const route of routes) {
64	      if (route.match(req.url)) return route.handler(req);
65	    }
66	    throw new Error(`fetch mock: no route for ${req.url}`);
67	  };
68	
69	  return Object.assign(fn, {
70	    calls,
71	    when(matcher: string | RegExp, handler: RouteHandler) {
72	      const match =
73	        typeof matcher === "string"
74	          ? (url: string) => url.includes(matcher)
75	          : (url: string) => matcher.test(url);
76	      routes.push({ match, handler });
77	    },

79	      return calls

82	    },
83	  });
84	}

type: epic
status: planning
created: 2026-10-20
---

# Migrate APOD source to science.nasa.gov

**Priority: P1.** Production is serving the NASA logo instead of the Astronomy Picture of the Day.

## Problem

NASA moved APOD from apod.nasa.gov to science.nasa.gov. The APOD editor announced the move for August/September 2026, and a third party reports the cutover on 2026-09-29. Everything this Worker depends on broke:

- `api.nasa.gov/planetary/apod` returns 200 with `title: "NASA Science"` and `url`/`hdurl` set to `https://science.nasa.gov/wp-content/themes/nasa-child/assets/images/nasa-logo@2x.png` for every date checked. Only `explanation` is still correct.
- `apod.nasa.gov/apod/` and every dated `apYYMMDD.html` page 301-redirect to the `science.nasa.gov/apod/` index, so the scrape fallback (TASK-0020, dev only) can't reach a specific date.
- The `nasa/apod-api` README ("Final update 9-10-2026") says that repo will be archived and api.nasa.gov pointed at the new endpoint on 2026-12-01. The old API is not coming back in its old form.

Observed in production on 2026-10-20:
- `/sd` serves the logo PNG (8,928 B).
- `/info` reports the "NASA Science" title.
- `/optimized` and `/thumb` return 502.
- `/` timed out.

Why our code accepted it: the logo response is a 200 with `media_type: "image"` and a `*.nasa.gov` URL. It passes `res.ok`, `resolveApod`, and `ALLOWED_IMAGE_HOSTS`. Nothing validates content, so it was cached in both tiers (6h primary, 24h stale) under date-only keys.

## Approach

This is a permanent migration to NASA's new official endpoint. No temporary workarounds, and no relying on cached data to cover the gap.

- Replace api.nasa.gov with the science.nasa.gov `apod-basic` WordPress REST API, which needs no key.
- Validate upstream data at the boundary, so a bad upstream response is never cached or served.
- Remove the apod.nasa.gov scrape, which has no working target.
- Version cache keys so nothing cached from the old source is ever read again.

## Source facts (verified 2026-10-20)

**Endpoint**
- Single date: `GET https://science.nasa.gov/wp-json/wp/v2/apod-basic/YYMMDD` (for example `261020`).
  - An unpublished date returns 404 `{"code":"apod_basic_not_found"}`.
  - A malformed date returns 400 `rest_invalid_param`.
  - The archive goes back to 1995.
- Range: `?date_from=YYMMDD&date_to=YYMMDD` returns newest first. ISO dates are rejected with 400.
- With no args, the list returns newest first (`x-wp-total: 11442`).
- `_fields=` trims the response, for example 256 B instead of 11 KB without `basic_html`.

**Fields**
- `date`: ISO.
- `title`.
- `media_type`.
- `explanation`: HTML, prefixed with `<strong>Explanation: </strong>`.
- `credit` and `copyright`: HTML, and identical in every sample.
- `alt`.
- `hdurl`.
- `permalink`.
- `url`: now equals `permalink`. It is **not** an image.
- `basic_html`: legacy APOD-layout HTML.
- `post_id`.

**Publishing and images**
- A new APOD publishes at 00:05 ET (`article:published_time`), which matches our ET date keys.
- Images live on `assets.science.nasa.gov`:
  - **Original:** `/content/dam/science/cds/apod/apod/YYYY/<month>/<file>`. It ignores query strings. Per nasa/apod-api#183 it is byte-identical to the old apod.nasa.gov originals.
  - **`hdurl` for recent dates:** `/dynamicimage/assets/science/cds/apod/...?w=...`, a re-encoded copy. The two paths map directly: `dynamicimage/assets/science/...` to `content/dam/science/...`.
  - **`dynamicimage` with no params:** 1280px default. `?w=N` is honored up to the original width; `fm` and `q` are ignored.
- Some archive entries have a placeholder `hdurl` (`.../cosmic-origins/images/misc/news-thumbnail.png`). Their real image is only in `basic_html`.

**Video days**
- YouTube: `media_type: "video"`, and `hdurl` is a poster still on assets.science.nasa.gov. The embed URL is only in `basic_html` (`<iframe src="//www.youtube.com/embed/...">`).
- Self-hosted MP4: `hdurl: ""`, and `basic_html` has `<video><source src=".../X.mp4">`.

**Caching and limits**
- wp-json sends `max-age=60`; assets send `max-age=43200`.
- robots.txt allows `/wp-json/`.
- No rate-limit headers were observed.

**Other notes**
- RSS (`https://science.nasa.gov/feed/apod-basic/`) and the permalink pages serve the same data from the same WordPress origin, so they are not independent fallbacks.
- Known upstream issues:
  - nasa/apod-api#179: HTML in fields, `url` repurposed, no video field.
  - #181: date params.
  - #183: re-encoded `hdurl`.
  - #184: logo.

## Tasks

1. **TASK-0042** [P1]: Fetch APOD metadata from the science.nasa.gov apod-basic API
2. **TASK-0043** [P1]: Resolve APOD image and video URLs from apod-basic data (blocked by TASK-0042)
3. **TASK-0044** [P1]: Remove the apod.nasa.gov scrape fallback (blocked by TASK-0042)
4. **TASK-0045** [P1]: Version cache keys so pre-migration entries are never read
5. **TASK-0046** [P1]: Update docs and user-facing text for the science.nasa.gov source (blocked by TASK-0042, TASK-0043, TASK-0044)
6. **TASK-0047** [P1]: Merge and deploy the APOD source migration to production (blocked by all of the above)

## Sequence

1. TASK-0042 first. It defines the fetch, validation, and internal model.
2. TASK-0043 and TASK-0044 in parallel.
3. TASK-0045 can land any time before TASK-0047.
4. TASK-0046.
5. TASK-0047.

## Cross-EPIC dependencies

These items assume the old source and need revisiting after this epic ships. None of them block it.

- **TASK-0021** (cron cache warming, EPIC-0003): it would currently warm caches with the logo, and it references `findLatestImage` (now `findLatestResolvable`).
- **TASK-0011** (R2 archive): its `{date}/hd.{ext}` / `{date}/sd.{ext}` keys assume the old hd/sd pair. It would currently archive the logo permanently.
- **TASK-0027** copy cites DEMO_KEY's 30 req/hr limit. **TASK-0032** mentions the `NASA_API_KEY` secret. **TASK-0003** says "we proxy the APOD API".
- **NOTE-0027** (download filename) parses apod.nasa.gov `/apod/image/YYMM/` URLs. The `content/dam` paths carry the original filename.
- **REFE-0001** dev-mode table (`nasa-error`, `video`, `video-no-thumb`).
- **Monitoring:** nothing alerted on this outage. NOTE-0029 (Sentry) or an upstream sanity alert would catch the next silent upstream change.
```

33:   - 404 `apod_basic_not_found` means "not published yet". Treat it as unresolvable so the walkback moves to the previous day. It is not an upstream failure, and nothing is cached for it. This covers the 00:00 to 00:05 ET window before NASA publishes.

Exit code 1
# NASA Picture Proxy

A Cloudflare Worker that proxies [NASA's Astronomy Picture of the Day (APOD)](https://science.nasa.gov/apod/) behind a fixed URL. An HTTP GET request returns today's image without needing an API key or parsing JSON.

[nasapicture.com](https://nasapicture.com) · [GitHub](https://github.com/GDKeller/nasa-picture-proxy)

![Today's APOD](https://api.nasapicture.com/image-sd.jpg)
*This is a static URL, but it'll be a different image when you visit this repo tomorrow.*

During a tinkering session, I wanted to set the background image of my homelab [homepage](https://github.com/gethomepage/homepage) dashboard to the APOD. I didn't want to inject additional JavaScript on the page and couldn't find an existing static URL. So, I built this proxy to share with anyone else who'd like to view the wonders of space easily, anywhere.


## Usage

Embed directly as an image:

```html
<img src="https://api.nasapicture.com/" alt="NASA Astronomy Picture of the Day" />
```

CSS background:

```css
body {
  background-image: url("https://api.nasapicture.com/");
  background-size: cover;
}
```

**Need a file extension?** Some contexts (RSS feeds, Open Graph tags, markdown renderers) require a URL that ends in an image extension. You can add `/image.jpg` or `/image-sd.jpg` as well:  
```
https://api.nasapicture.com/image.jpg
https://api.nasapicture.com/image-sd.jpg
```  

Fetch metadata:

```bash
curl https://api.nasapicture.com/info | jq .
```

Returns the day's APOD record from NASA's science.nasa.gov feed:
- Direct URLs of APOD images (and the video, on video days)
- Date
- Image title
- Image explanation
- Copyright info
- Link to the APOD article on science.nasa.gov

> [!TIP]
> For those without the tech savvy to understand (i.e. remember) "api", all routes are also accessible at `get.nasapicture.com`

## Endpoints

| Path | Response |
|------|----------|
| `/` | Today's APOD image (HD, falls back to standard) |
| `/image.jpg` | Same as `/` with file extension |
| `/sd` | Standard resolution image |
| `/image-sd.jpg` | Same as `/sd` with file extension |
| `/optimized` | Optimized image (≤1200px, auto WebP/AVIF) |
| `/image-optimized.jpg` | Same as `/optimized` with file extension |
| `/thumb` | Tiny blurred thumbnail (32px WebP, ~1KB) |
| `/thumb.jpg` | Same as `/thumb` with file extension |
| `/info` | JSON metadata (title, date, explanation, copyright, image and article URLs, image dimensions) |
| `/about` | Plain-text description and route listing |

When the APOD of the day is a video, the proxy serves NASA's poster image for it, and `/info` returns the video's URL. If the video has no poster, it walks backwards up to 7 days to find the most recent image.

## How it works

The Worker fetches each day's record from NASA's `apod-basic` feed on science.nasa.gov. "Today" is the date in `America/New_York`, so it rolls over at midnight ET. If NASA hasn't published today's entry yet, the proxy serves yesterday's.

The record and the image bytes are cached with the Workers Cache API (`caches.default`) for 6 hours. A second copy is kept for 24 hours and served if NASA's site is down. Cache keys carry a version, so a change of source or format never serves an entry cached by an older one. There's no KV, D1, or cron involved.

## Author

Built by [Grant Keller](https://grantkeller.dev).

---
type: reference
created: 2026-04-09

# Dev feature flag convention

Cross-project shared convention for dev/debug toggles. Originated in conversations between NASA Picture Proxy and the portfolio project; this file is the local copy of the spec. All new dev/debug hooks in this repo MUST follow it.

## The distinction

Dev flags come in two fundamentally different shapes. Cramming both into one slot creates friction — modes steal the slot tools need, or tools pollute the modes dimension. Keep them separate.

- **Mode** — single-value render state. **One at a time. Mutually exclusive.** Examples: `fallback`, `stale`, `video`, `nasa-error`, `offline`.
- **Tools** — set of independent helper overlays. **Any combination on at once. Additive.** Examples: `palette`, `grid`, `cache-inspector`, `fps`.

## The convention

| Purpose | Query param | localStorage key | Shape | Example |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Render mode | `?dev=<name>` | `dev-mode` | single value | `?dev=stale`, `?dev=off` |
| Helper tools | `?tools=<a,b,c>` | `dev-tools` | comma set | `?tools=palette,grid` |

## Semantics (declarative)

- The URL value is always the **complete desired state** for that dimension.
- **Modes:** `?dev=stale` replaces the current mode. `?dev=off` or `?dev=` clears it.
- **Tools:** `?tools=palette,grid` replaces the tool set entirely with `{palette, grid}`. `?tools=` clears the set.
- If a query param is **absent from the URL**, the stored localStorage value is **left untouched** — navigating to a clean URL does not lose your dev state.
- Both dimensions persist to localStorage on sync, so the query param only needs to appear **once per browser** to "stick."

## Programmatic escape hatch (browser)

When you can't or don't want to modify the URL:

```js
localStorage.setItem("dev-mode", "stale");
localStorage.setItem("dev-tools", "palette,grid");
// clear
localStorage.removeItem("dev-mode");
localStorage.removeItem("dev-tools");
```

## Reference implementation

A small vanilla-JS/TS module lives at `landing/src/lib/dev-flags.ts` (or wherever the landing build puts it). Small enough to copy-paste across projects — not published as a package yet.

Exposes:

- `getDevMode(): string | null` — current mode, or `null` if none set
- `getDevTools(): Set<string>` — current enabled tool set
- `hasTool(name: string): boolean` — convenience check
- `syncDevFlagsFromUrl(): void` — read URL params, mirror into localStorage. Call once at the top of the client script before reading flags.

### Usage pattern

```ts
import { syncDevFlagsFromUrl, hasTool, getDevMode } from "./lib/dev-flags";

syncDevFlagsFromUrl();

if (getDevMode() === "stale") {
  // force the stale-image fallback state
}
if (hasTool("palette")) {
  // reveal the palette picker overlay
}
```

## Worker-side (server)

Workers don't have localStorage or persistence between requests, so the "sticky" part of the spec only applies to browser clients. For the Worker (`src/index.ts`) the contract is:

- Read `?dev=<mode>` and `?tools=<csv>` from the request URL on each request
- Parse once at the entry point into a single `devFlags` object; everything downstream reads from that object (same "gate at the boundary" principle)
- **Gating:** only honor dev params when an env-driven flag is set. Preferred approach is reading `env.ENVIRONMENT === "development"` from `.dev.vars` (gitignored). Unset env is treated as production. Dev params on a production request are silently ignored.

The mode/tool **names** and kebab-case conventions are the same as browser-side.

## Naming

Short, scenario-oriented, kebab-case:

| Good | Bad |
|---|---|
| `?dev=video` | `?dev=force-video-thumbnail-branch` |
| `?dev=nasa-error` | `?dev=force-nasa-500` |
| `?tools=palette` | `?tools=show-theme-palette-overlay` |

Avoid implementation details in the name. `video` is a scenario; `force-video-thumbnail-branch` leaks internals.

## Current modes and tools (NASA Picture Proxy)

### Landing (`landing/index.html`)

| Param | Description |
|---|---|
| `?dev=fallback` | Force the "image not available" fallback state |
| `?dev=stale` | Simulate showing a previous day's image as fallback |

> Landing currently uses the `?dev=` query param but **does not persist to `dev-mode` localStorage** and **does not honor `?dev=off` as a clear**. Retrofit tracked in TASK-0036.

### Worker (`src/index.ts`)

Gated on `env.ENVIRONMENT === "development"` (set in `.dev.vars`, gitignored). If the env var is unset or any other value, dev params are silently ignored and all requests go through the normal path.

| Param | Task | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `?dev=video` | TASK-0019 | Return a hard-coded video APOD fixture *with* `thumbnail_url` so the video-thumbnail branch of `resolveApod` can be exercised. Only short-circuits for today's date; walkback iterations still hit the normal path. Bypasses the APOD cache entirely so fixture runs never pollute real cached data. |
| `?dev=video-no-thumb` | TASK-0019 | Return a hard-coded video APOD fixture *without* `thumbnail_url`. `resolveApod` returns null for today, so the walkback path runs and pulls the next resolvable day. |
| `?dev=nasa-error` | TASK-0020, TASK-0044 | Skip the upstream APOD fetch and simulate an upstream failure: serve the stale cache entry if present, otherwise 502. Bypasses the primary cache so every request reliably exercises the fallback. The apod.nasa.gov scrape that used to follow the stale check was removed in EPIC-0006. |

## Why this shape

- **Separate namespaces for exclusive vs. additive toggles.** Trying to combine two modes is nonsensical; combining two tools is natural. Splitting them keeps the semantics honest.
- **Kebab-case CSVs** are URL-safe and don't need escaping.
- **Declarative URL + sticky localStorage** means one link shared with someone can set their state, but navigating away doesn't clobber it.
- **Single registry.** This file is the authoritative list of dev modes and tools across NASA Picture Proxy. When you add a new one, add it here too.

## Prior art and sibling projects

- **Portfolio** — palette picker overlay originated the `?tools=` pattern (was previously `?palette=1` + `palette-picker` key; retrofit 2026-04-09)
- **NASA Picture Proxy (this repo)** — originated the `?dev=fallback` / `?dev=stale` mode shape. Landing page retrofit to the full shared convention (localStorage + `off` clear) tracked in TASK-0036.

## Open questions

- Third dimension for typed config values (e.g. `?config=delay:500,region:us-west`)? For now, piggyback on mode names like `?dev=slow-500` if needed — avoid premature dimension creep.
- Shared npm package? Not yet — the module is small enough to copy-paste, and each project stays free to evolve independently. Revisit if 3+ projects adopt and drift becomes a problem.

## Housekeeping

When a new dev mode or tool is added to the code, update the "Current modes and tools" tables above in the same change. This doc is the canonical registry for this repo.

          dateEl.setAttribute('datetime', data.date);
          dateEl.title = 'NASA publishes on Eastern Time';
          document.getElementById('hero-caption').classList.add('visible');
        }

        // Pre-size container with aspect ratio from dimensions
        if (data.width && data.height) {
          wrapper.style.aspectRatio = `${data.width} / ${data.height}`;
        }

        // Show stale notice if image is from a previous day
        const todayET = new Date().toLocaleDateString('en-CA', { timeZone: 'America/New_York' });
        if (devFlag === 'stale' || data.date !== todayET) {
          showStaleNotice();
        }
      }

      // Show scaled-up thumbnail as placeholder
      if (thumbUrl) {
        wrapper.style.backgroundImage = `url(${thumbUrl})`;
        wrapper.classList.add('has-thumb');
      }
    });

For example, a GIF with 500x500 dimensions and 10 frames has an image area of 2,500,000 pixels or 2.5 megapixels.\n\n\n### Limits for animated images\n\nGIF/WebP animations are limited to the total megapixels across all frames, or the sum of areas of all frames. For example, a GIF with 500x500 dimensions and 10 frames has an image area of 2,500,000 pixels or 2.5 megapixels.\n\nThe limit to deliver an animated GIF/WebP animation is 100 megapixels. However, any animations over 50 megapixels will be delivered without applying any transformations.\n\nWhen serving animations, we recommend using video formats like MP4 and WebM for best performance. As the GIF format has inefficient compression, high resolution animations typically have larger file sizes and take longer to compress.\n\nTo optimize remote videos, you can use [media transformations ↗](https://developers.cloudflare.com/stream/transform-videos/).\n\n### Limits for the Images binding\n\nWhen optimizing with the [Images binding](/images/optimization/binding/), the maximum input size for `.input()` is 20 MB.\n\n## Supported formats\n\n### Input formats\n\nImages supports a wide range of input formats for both remote and hosted images:\n\n* PNG\n* JPEG\n* GIF (including animations)\n* WebP (including animations)\n* SVG\n* AVIF\\*\n* HEIC\n\n\\*Available on an Enterprise plan.\n\n### Output formats\n\n"},{"similarity":0.7619045972824097,"id":"d5d0f9b092d22cdc04bd876d3638d76d56d82aab9fe03a9438bb29cb23965ce2","url":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/images/reference/troubleshooting/","title":"Troubleshooting","text":"## Limits\n\nThese are the limits for images that are stored outside of Images:\n\n* Maximum image size is 100 megapixels (for example, 10,000×10,000 pixels large). Maximum file size is 100 megabytes (MB). GIF/WebP animations are limited to 50 megapixels total (sum of sizes of all frames).\n* [Bring Your Own IP (BYOIP)](/byoip/) is not compatible with Images when optimizing remote images (transformations).\n* When [Polish](/images/polish/) can't optimize an image the Response Header `Warning: cf-images 299 \"original is smaller\"` is returned.\n\n---\n\n## Authorization and cookies are not supported\n\nImage requests to the origin will be anonymized (no cookies, no auth, no custom headers). This is because we have to have one public cache for resized images, and it would be unsafe to share images that are personalized for individual visitors.\n\nHowever, in cases where customers agree to store such images in public cache, Cloudflare supports resizing images through Workers [on authenticated origins](/images/optimization/transformations/transform-via-workers/).\n\n---\n\n## Caching and purging\n\nChanges to image dimensions or other resizing options always take effect immediately — no purging necessary.\n\n\n.\n* 9413 — The image exceeds the maximum image area of 100 megapixels. The following API calls count toward this limit while the initial connection is being established and the server has not yet responded:\n\n* `fetch()` method of the [Fetch API](/workers/runtime-apis/fetch/)\n* `get()`, `put()`, `list()`, and `delete()` methods of [Workers KV namespace objects](/kv/api/)\n* `put()`, `match()`, and `delete()` methods of [Cache objects](/workers/runtime-apis/cache/)\n* `list()`, `get()`, `put()`, `delete()`, and `head()` methods of [R2](/r2/)\n* `send()` and `sendBatch()` methods of [Queues](/queues/)\n* Opening a TCP socket using the [connect()](/workers/runtime-apis/tcp-sockets/) API\n\nOutbound WebSocket connections also count toward this limit.\n\nOnce response headers arrive for a connection, it no longer counts toward the six-connection limit. async function findLatestImage(log: string[], apiKey: string): Promise<ApodResponse> {
  let videos = 0;
  let errors = 0;

  for (let i = 0; i <= MAX_LOOKBACK_DAYS; i++) {
    const d = new Date();
    d.setDate(d.getDate() - i);
    const date = d.toLocaleDateString("en-CA", { timeZone: "America/New_York" });

    try {
      const apod = await fetchApod(log, apiKey, date);
      if (apod.media_type === "image") return apod;
      videos++;
    } catch (err) {
      errors++;
      const msg = err instanceof Error ? err.message : "unknown";
      log.push(`  [findLatestImage] ${date} → error, skipping (${msg})`);
    }
  }

  throw new Error(
    `No image found in last ${MAX_LOOKBACK_DAYS + 1} days (${videos} videos, ${errors} errors)`
  );
}

function validateImageUrl(url: string): void {
  const parsed = new URL(url);
  if (parsed.protocol !== "https:") {
    throw new Error(`Blocked image fetch: non-HTTPS scheme (${parsed.protocol})`);
  }
  if (!parsed.hostname.endsWith(".nasa.gov")) {
    throw new Error(`Blocked image fetch: unexpected host (${parsed.hostname})`);
  }
}

async function fetchImageCached(log: string[], url: string): Promise<Response> {
  validateImageUrl(url);

  const cache = caches.default;
  const cacheReq = new Request(`https://api.nasapicture.com/_cache/image/${encodeURIComponent(url)}`);
  const staleReq = new Request(`https://api.nasapicture.com/_cache/image/${encodeURIComponent(url)}:stale`);

  const cached = await cache.match(cacheReq);
  if (cached) {
    log.push(`  [fetchImage] ${url.slice(0, 80)}… → cache HIT`);
    return cached;
  }

  const res = await fetch(url);

  log.push(`  [fetchImage] ${url.slice(0, 80)}… → ${res.status}`);

  if (!res.ok) {
    // Try stale cache before giving up
    const stale = await cache.match(staleReq);
    if (stale) {
      log.push(`  [fetchImage] ${url.slice(0, 80)}… → stale cache fallback`);
      return stale;
    }
    throw new Error(`Image fetch failed: ${res.status}`);
  }

  const contentType = res.headers.get("Content-Type") || "image/jpeg";
  const contentLength = res.headers.get("Content-Length");
  const cacheHeaders: Record<string, string> = {
    "Content-Type": contentType,
    "Cache-Control": `public, max-age=${CACHE_TTL}`,
  };
  if (contentLength) cacheHeaders["Content-Length"] = contentLength;

  const staleCacheHeaders = { ...cacheHeaders, "Cache-Control": `public, max-age=${STALE_CACHE_TTL}` };

  const arrayBuffer = await res.arrayBuffer();
  await Promise.all([
    cache.put(cacheReq, new Response(arrayBuffer, { headers: cacheHeaders })),
    cache.put(staleReq, new Response(arrayBuffer, { headers: staleCacheHeaders })),
  ]);
  return new Response(arrayBuffer, { headers: cacheHeaders });
}

interface ImageDimensions {
  width: number;
  height: number;
}

async function fetchImageDimensions(log: string[], imageUrl: string): Promise<ImageDimensions | null> {
  validateImageUrl(imageUrl);

  const cache = caches.default;
  const cacheKey = `https://api.nasapicture.com/_cache/dimensions/${encodeURIComponent(imageUrl)}`;
  const cacheReq = new Request(cacheKey);
  const staleReq = new Request(`${cacheKey}:stale`);

  const cached = await cache.match(cacheReq);
  if (cached) {
    log.push(`  [dimensions] ${imageUrl.slice(0, 80)}… → cache HIT`);
    return cached.json() as Promise<ImageDimensions>;
  }

  try {
    const res = await fetch(imageUrl, {
      cf: { image: { format: "json" } },
    });

    if (!res.ok) {
      const stale = await cache.match(staleReq);
      if (stale) {
        log.push(`  [dimensions] ${imageUrl.slice(0, 80)}… → stale cache fallback`);
        return stale.json() as Promise<ImageDimensions>;
      }
      log.push(`  [dimensions] ${imageUrl.slice(0, 80)}… → ${res.status} (failed)`);
      return null;
    }

    const info = await res.json() as { original: { width: number; height: number } };
    const dimensions: ImageDimensions = {
      width: info.original.width,
      height: info.original.height,
    };

    log.push(`  [dimensions] ${imageUrl.slice(0, 80)}… → ${dimensions.width}×${dimensions.height}`);

    const body = JSON.stringify(dimensions);
    await Promise.all([
      cache.put(cacheReq, new Response(body, {
        headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json", "Cache-Control": `public, max-age=${CACHE_TTL}` },
      })),
      cache.put(staleReq, new Response(body, {
        headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json", "Cache-Control": `public, max-age=${STALE_CACHE_TTL}` },
      })),
    ]);
    return dimensions;
  } catch (err) {
    log.push(`  [dimensions] ${imageUrl.slice(0, 80)}… → error: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : "unknown"}`);
    const stale = await cache.match(staleReq);
    if (stale) return stale.json() as Promise<ImageDimensions>;
    return null;
  }
}

function baseHeaders(origin: string, headers: Record<string, string> = {}): Record<string, string> {
  return {
    "Access-Control-Allow-Origin": "*",
    "Cache-Control": `public, max-age=${CACHE_TTL}`,
    "Link": [
      `<${origin}/>; rel="alternate"; type="image/*"; title="HD image"`,
      `<${origin}/sd>; rel="alternate"; type="image/*"; title="SD image"`,
      `<${origin}/optimized>; rel="alternate"; type="image/*"; title="Optimized image"`,

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Project Overview

APOD Proxy — a Cloudflare Worker that proxies NASA's Astronomy Picture of the Day behind stable, fixed URLs. The source is the keyless `apod-basic` WordPress REST API on science.nasa.gov (see EPIC-0006 for its field behavior).

## Commands

- `npm run dev` starts the API (localhost:8787) and landing page (localhost:8788) in the background. Check them with `npm run status`, stop them with `npm run stop`, and read logs with the `npm run log:*` scripts.
- Type-check with `npx tsc --noEmit`. There is no build artifact; Wrangler bundles `src/` directly.

## Architecture

Caching uses the Workers Cache API (`caches.default`) with a two-tier strategy — no KV, D1, or cron:
- **Primary cache** (6h TTL): APOD metadata keyed by ET date, image bytes keyed by NASA URL
- **Stale fallback** (24h TTL): same data under a `:stale` suffixed key, served when the apod-basic source fails

Cache keys are date-based in `America/New_York` timezone, so they roll over at midnight ET. Every key starts with `CACHE_BASE` (`/_cache/v2`); bump its version whenever the cached shape or upstream source changes. Cache key URLs must use a zone-scoped hostname (`https://api.nasapicture.com/_cache/...`), not synthetic hostnames -- `caches.default` silently drops writes for unknown hosts.

The landing page (`landing/`) is served at `nasapicture.com` via Cloudflare Pages. The Worker serves `api.nasapicture.com` and `get.nasapicture.com`. Brand voice and design context live in `landing/CLAUDE.md`; read it before writing user-facing copy anywhere, including the Worker's `/about` text.

## Environment

- No secrets. The APOD source needs no API key.
- Local vars go in `.dev.vars` (gitignored).

import { describe, it, expect, beforeEach, afterEach, vi } from "vitest";
import worker, { __resetInflightApod, apodCacheUrl, normalizeApod } from "../src/index";

// ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// In-memory stand-ins for globals the Worker reaches for. Node gives us
// Request/Response/fetch/URL natively; we only need to fake `caches.default`
// and route outbound `fetch` calls. The tests call the default export's
// fetch handler directly — no wrangler, no miniflare, no real network.
// ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

interface CacheEntry {
  body: ArrayBuffer;
  headers: [string, string][];
}

function createCache() {
  const store = new Map<string, CacheEntry>();
  const cache = {
    async match(req: Request | string): Promise<Response | undefined> {
      const url = typeof req === "string" ? req : req.url;
      const entry = store.get(url);
      if (!entry) return undefined;
      return new Response(entry.body.slice(0), { headers: entry.headers });
    },
    async put(req: Request | string, res: Response): Promise<void> {
      const url = typeof req === "string" ? req : req.url;
      const body = await res.arrayBuffer();
      const headers: [string, string][] = [];
      res.headers.forEach((value, key) => headers.push([key, value]));
      store.set(url, { body, headers });
    },
    async delete(req: Request | string): Promise<boolean> {
      const url = typeof req === "string" ? req : req.url;
      return store.delete(url);
    },
    // helpers for assertions
    _keys: () => Array.from(store.keys()),
    _size: () => store.size,
  };
  return cache;
}

type CacheMock = ReturnType<typeof createCache>;

interface FetchCall {
  url: string;
  method: string;
  userAgent: string | null;
}

type RouteHandler = (req: Request) => Response | Promise<Response>;

function createFetchMock() {
  const routes: Array<{ match: (url: string) => boolean; handler: RouteHandler }> = [];
  const calls: FetchCall[] = [];

  const fn: typeof fetch = async (input, init) => {
    const req =
      input instanceof Request
        ? new Request(input, init)
        : new Request(typeof input === "string" ? input : String(input), init);
    calls.push({ url: req.url, method: req.method, userAgent: req.headers.get("User-Agent") });
    for (const route of routes) {
      if (route.match(req.url)) return route.handler(req);
    }
    throw new Error(`fetch mock: no route for ${req.url}`);
  };

  return Object.assign(fn, {
    calls,
    when(matcher: string | RegExp, handler: RouteHandler) {
      const match =
        typeof matcher === "string"
          ? (url: string) => url.includes(matcher)
          : (url: string) => matcher.test(url);
      routes.push({ match, handler });
    },
    urlsMatching(pattern: string | RegExp): string[] {
      return calls
        .map((c) => c.url)
        .filter((u) => (typeof pattern === "string" ? u.includes(pattern) : pattern.test(u)));
    },
  });
}

type FetchMock = ReturnType<typeof createFetchMock>;

// ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// Test harness state
// ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

let cache: CacheMock;
let fetchMock: FetchMock;
let originalFetch: typeof fetch | undefined;
let originalCaches: typeof caches | undefined;

const DEV_ENV = { ENVIRONMENT: "development" };
const PROD_ENV = {};

// Pin "now" to a deterministic instant so todayET() always returns 2026-04-10.
// 16:00 UTC on 2026-04-10 is 12:00 ET — safely inside the same ET day.
const PINNED_NOW = new Date("2026-04-10T16:00:00Z");
const TODAY = "2026-04-10";
const YESTERDAY = "2026-04-09";

beforeEach(() => {
  vi.useFakeTimers();
  vi.setSystemTime(PINNED_NOW);

  cache = createCache();
  fetchMock = createFetchMock();

  originalFetch = globalThis.fetch;
  originalCaches = (globalThis as unknown as { caches?: typeof caches }).caches;

  (globalThis as unknown as { fetch: typeof fetch }).fetch = fetchMock;
  (globalThis as unknown as { caches: { default: CacheMock } }).caches = {
    default: cache,
  };

  __resetInflightApod();
});

afterEach(() => {
  vi.useRealTimers();
  if (originalFetch) {
    (globalThis as unknown as { fetch: typeof fetch }).fetch = originalFetch;
  }
  if (originalCaches) {
    (globalThis as unknown as { caches: typeof caches }).caches = originalCaches;
  } else {
    delete (globalThis as unknown as { caches?: unknown }).caches;
  }
});

  const cache = caches.default;
  const cacheReq = new Request(`https://api.nasapicture.com/_cache/image/${encodeURIComponent(url)}`);
  const staleReq = new Request(`https://api.nasapicture.com/_cache/image/${encodeURIComponent(url)}:stale`);

  const cached = await cache.match(cacheReq);
  if (cached) {
    log.push(`  [fetchImage] ${url.slice(0, 80)}… → cache HIT`);
    return cached;
  }

  const res = await fetch(url);

  log.push(`  [fetchImage] ${url.slice(0, 80)}… → ${res.status}`);

  if (!res.ok) {
    // Try stale cache before giving up
    const stale = await cache.match(staleReq);
    if (stale) {
      log.push(`  [fetchImage] ${url.slice(0, 80)}… → stale cache fallback`);
      return stale;
    }
    throw new Error(`Image fetch failed: ${res.status}`);
  }

  const contentType = res.headers.get("Content-Type") || "image/jpeg";
  const contentLength = res.headers.get("Content-Length");
  const cacheHeaders: Record<string, string> = {
    "Content-Type": contentType,
    "Cache-Control": `public, max-age=${CACHE_TTL}`,
  };
  if (contentLength) cacheHeaders["Content-Length"] = contentLength;

  const staleCacheHeaders = { ...cacheHeaders, "Cache-Control": `public, max-age=${STALE_CACHE_TTL}` };

  const arrayBuffer = await res.arrayBuffer();
  await Promise.all([
    cache.put(cacheReq, new Response(arrayBuffer, { headers: cacheHeaders })),
    cache.put(staleReq, new Response(arrayBuffer, { headers: staleCacheHeaders })),
  ]);
  return new Response(arrayBuffer, { headers: cacheHeaders });
}

Exit code 1
---
type: epic
status: planning
created: 2026-10-20
